section_summary.extract_value: This Results section presents the validation and psychometric properties of the BAS-2 (Body Appreciation Scale-2) using a single study with a combined sample of 675 participants (split into EFA Group 1, n=338, and EFA Group 2, n=337, for cross-validation). The analysis revealed a unidimensional 10-item BAS-2 scale with strong internal consistency (Cronbach's alphas .93–.94) and test–retest reliability (ICCs = .90). The BAS-2 demonstrated strong construct validity and criterion-related validity, with significant negative correlations with BMI (overall r = –.27; women r = –.23, men r = –.32, all ps < .001), and incremental validity in predicting eating behavior and psychological well-being beyond appearance evaluation and body dissatisfaction.
section_summary.evidence_source: Entire Results section synthesized from preliminary analyses through incremental validity findings.
